name: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
aliases: unexplained cardiac arrest with normal heart

reference.source: Standard cardiology and inherited cardiac conditions references
clinicalPearls: A diagnosis of exclusion applied to resuscitated ventricular fibrillation when no structural, electrical, metabolic or toxic cause is identified after thorough evaluation
Requires systematic exclusion of coronary disease, cardiomyopathy, and inherited channelopathies such as long QT, Brugada, and catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Often triggered by short-coupled ventricular ectopy, sometimes arising from the Purkinje system or right ventricular outflow tract
A short-coupled variant with very early ectopic beats initiating fibrillation is recognised as a distinct high-risk entity
Typically affects young, otherwise healthy adults presenting with aborted sudden death, so meticulous family and genetic evaluation is essential
Because a subtle inherited cause may only declare itself later, ongoing surveillance and cascade family screening are important
Secondary prevention with an implantable defibrillator is standard for survivors of the arrest
reference.pathophysiology: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation denotes a primary electrical disorder of the heart in which ventricular fibrillation occurs without demonstrable structural, ischaemic or recognised channelopathic cause. In many patients, closely coupled ventricular premature beats, frequently originating from Purkinje tissue or a ventricular outflow region, fall on the vulnerable phase of repolarisation and degenerate into fibrillation. Underlying microscopic or as-yet-unrecognised ion-channel or repolarisation abnormalities are presumed, and some patients are later reclassified once a concealed channelopathy or cardiomyopathy becomes apparent. The label therefore reflects the current limits of investigation rather than a single defined mechanism.
additionalDifferentials: Occult ischaemic or structural heart disease (including subtle cardiomyopathy)
additionalInvestigations: 12-lead ECG with repeated and high-lead recordings to seek a concealed channelopathy
Echocardiography and cardiac MRI to exclude structural disease
Coronary evaluation and provocation testing to exclude ischaemia and vasospasm
Drug-provocation and exercise testing to unmask Brugada or catecholaminergic phenotypes
Genetic testing and comprehensive cascade family screening
Ambulatory monitoring to characterise triggering ectopy and its coupling interval
redFlags: Recurrent ventricular fibrillation or electrical storm
Very short-coupled premature beats initiating fibrillation
Family history of unexplained sudden death or aborted arrest
Emergence of a diagnostic channelopathy pattern on follow-up
reference.prognosis: Survivors face an ongoing risk of recurrent malignant arrhythmia, mitigated by defibrillator therapy; long-term outlook depends on whether a specific underlying disorder is subsequently identified and treatable, and on control of triggering ectopy.
pitfalls: Settling on the label without an exhaustive search for a specific cause
Missing a concealed channelopathy that only manifests with provocation or over time
Neglecting cascade family screening for an inherited disorder
Overlooking short-coupled triggering ectopy amenable to targeted therapy
references: ESC guidelines on ventricular arrhythmias and prevention of sudden cardiac death
management: Implant a cardioverter-defibrillator as the cornerstone of secondary prevention after resuscitated ventricular fibrillation
Treat the arrest and any electrical storm with prompt defibrillation and advanced life support, using an isoprenaline infusion during storm
Suppress the closely coupled triggering ectopy with quinidine, which is particularly effective, and consider beta-blockers or verapamil
Offer catheter ablation of the initiating Purkinje or outflow-tract ectopic focus for recurrent arrhythmia or refractory electrical storm
Maintain long-term rhythm surveillance and periodic re-evaluation, as a concealed channelopathy or cardiomyopathy may later declare itself
Arrange genetic testing and cascade screening of first-degree relatives through an inherited cardiac conditions clinic
